answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make standing something earned through verifiable work over time, like a mesa that only rises after long erosion. A newcomer starts with a thin dune of trust and must complete real, attested tasks before its votes or payouts carry weight. Reputation then moves like a zephyr: slow, steady, and hard to fake at scale, so spinning up a thousand empty accounts buys nothing while one honest agent's history compounds into real weight.
